  • Classes in com.egradx.auth.security used by com.egradx.auth.config
    Class
    Description
    EgradxAccessDeniedHandler
    A signed-in caller refused by Spring Security (a failing @PreAuthorize on an application's own endpoint, with no @ControllerAdvice answering it first): 403 ACCESS_DENIED in the SDK's envelope, as Node's requireAuthority and Python's require_authority answer.
    EgradxAttemptLimiter
    Limits password guesses.
    EgradxAuthenticationEntryPoint
    The 401 for a request that needs a signed-in caller and has none, in the same envelope and with the same codes as egradx-auth's own endpoints: SESSION_EXPIRED when a bearer token was presented and refused, NOT_AUTHENTICATED when there was none.
    EgradxAuthenticationFilter
    Verifies the caller's bearer token, then — this is the part that matters — re-resolves their current identity/authorities from the database via EgradxPermissionResolver rather than trusting anything the token itself claims about roles or permissions (it doesn't carry any).
    EgradxPermissionResolver
    Resolves a user's current identity/organization/authorities from the database, deliberately ignoring whatever an access token's own claims say — this is what makes a role reassignment or a permission edit take effect on a user's very next request instead of their next login.
    EgradxTenantContextAccessor
    Access to the current request's EgradxTenantContext.

    EgradxAuthenticatedPrincipal
    Authentication.getPrincipal() for a request EgradxAuthenticationFilter has authenticated — a purpose-built record, not the raw EgradxUserEntity JPA entity, so a passwordHash or a lazily-loaded collection can never end up reachable from the security context.
